headline: New Scientist asks whether physics will be the next field to be transformed by AI.
score_reason: Lowered by 1: only New Scientist's question is known; the related benchmark report is a separate story.
importance_line: If AI can now solve research-level physics problems, as the benchmark authors report, it could change how physicists work, though the problems are what the authors call “turn-the-crank” research rather than groundbreaking discoveries.
summary: New Scientist asks on 16 Oct 2026 whether physics will be the next field to be turned upside down by AI. Separately, OfficeChai reported on 15 Oct 2026 on a new benchmark called TheoPhysEval, built by nearly 30 physicists from institutions including Harvard and Google DeepMind, in which OpenAI's GPT-6-Astra solved 49 of 50 new theoretical physics research problems.
notes: Headline only for the New Scientist piece; related context from OfficeChai (https://officechai.com/ai/gpt-6-astra-solves-49-50-unpublished-physics-research-problems-under-theophyseval-benchmark-for-3-a-problem/), a separate story. Desk-built entry.
